stories.notes: Spec already completed with both openspec and speckit. Coordinator review verdict is needs_review (quality 0.65) with flags: openspec_produced_no_draft_acs, speckit_derived_all_criteria_without_codebase_inspection, three_market_scope_insufficiently_decomposed, ac_elaboration_not_stakeholder_validated. Re-running agents would not resolve these gaps — human review is required first to validate derived ACs against real requirements and codebase state before any further spec work.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — Live Preview config stub exists in contentstack.ts (enable/host/management_token) but the runtime integration (reading live_preview query param, passing LivePreviewQuery to SDK calls, re-rendering on draft updates) is absent. useContent (236 callers) is the sole attachment point every content component flows through. GO/UP/MX share identical codepaths; decomposition is by env vars (CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST, CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN, CONTENTSTACK_API_KEY, CONTENTSTACK_DELIVERY_TOKEN, CONTENTSTACK_ENVIRONMENT) per market deployment — no code-level branching required. Flag 1 resolved: draft ACs produced. Flag 2 resolved: VCs derived from actual code symbols (useContent, contentstack.ts options, LivePreviewQuery contract). Flag 3 resolved: market decomposition is env-var-driven, same codepath. Flag 4 resolved: ACs are stakeholder-observable in the CMS preview pane.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Brownfield ticket — AC immutability and split constraints respected; not evaluating AC completeness or split quality. On agent value: openspec provided meaningful, non-overlapping context (identifying useContent as the 236-caller attachment point, env-var-driven market decomposition, and the LivePreviewQuery contract gap) but produced no draft acceptance criteria. Speckit is referenced in coordinator notes and is credited with deriving 12 ACs, yet it is absent from both appliedAgents and agentContributions — its contribution was either not formally recorded or not applied through the pipeline. This is a recording gap that obscures whether speckit actually ran or whether its output was incorporated by the coordinator retroactively. The derived criteria were produced without codebase inspection and lack stakeholder validation, creating misalignment risk for a three-market (GO, UP, MX) feature. Re-running agents will not resolve these issues; human review is required first to validate the derived ACs against real codebase state and stakeholder intent before further spec work proceeds.
